claude.rationale: The slice states the acquired product (real estate portfolio plus third-party asset-management contracts) was structured to "cross together with its producing processes and staff via a newly formed taxable REIT subsidiary" — the Property Manager entity, certain employees, and the investment-management agreements were all transferred to the Manager, so product (T4) and its producing processes (T5) moved coherently together (gap_45=0). Likewise, the operational staff/employees and management team moved alongside the processes into the Manager, with PECO I acquiring employees it had not previously had, so T5 and the organization/people (T6) transferred together (gap_56=0). The retention risk for key employees and the residual PELP legacy layer are noted but the deal structured product, process, and people to move as one bundle at closing; because no closing-structure gap is documented, gap_mitigated is NA (the Services Agreement bridges the retained residual, not a transfer gap in the acquired bundle). T1 owner intent continues (Edison and management keep roles and hold equity on both sides), converting external advisory into self-management, hence T2 swap and T3 whole transfer of the Contributed Companies as subsidiaries.

gemini.rationale: The slice explicitly states that the operational staff and management contracts that produced and delivered the asset-management product were structured to move together with the product itself into a newly formed taxable REIT subsidiary. Therefore, there is no structural mismatch between the product (T4) and processes (T5), nor between the processes (T5) and the organization/people (T6) at closing.

openai.rationale: The slice states that the contributed real estate, management contracts, Property Manager entity, operational staff, and certain employees were structured to move together into PECO I OP through the newly formed Manager, so no product-versus-process gap is documented at closing. It also states that the employees and management contracts producing the asset-management services transferred alongside those operations; employee-retention risk did not itself establish a closing mismatch between processes and organization. Retained PELP assets and legacy funds remained under PELP's operation and were supported by a Services Agreement, rather than being customer-facing assets transferred without their operating substrate.
